title: Release Curator: traffic sculptor and safety gates for progressive model rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a release curator component (internal name: Traffic Sculptor) that expresses progressive model rollouts with flexible step schedules, attribute-aware traffic splits (user cohort, region, priority), shadowing, and automated rollback/hold guardrails. The curator should be declarative (YAML/JSON DSL), integrate with the serving runtime router, and emit rich events for the Console and Alerting systems. This ticket covers API, runtime hooks, default safety gate presets, and integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: Curator DSL supports: percentage ramps, cohort-based splits, time-based and metric-based step progression
Runtime applies traffic decisions without request loss and supports shadowing (0% -> 100% simultaneous mirrored requests)
Guardrails: configurable P95 latency, error-rate, and quality-regression gates with auto-hold and auto-rollback behaviors
Console shows per-step metrics and allows manual step override (advance/hold/rollback)
E2E tests demonstrating automatic rollback on injected failure and successful promote on stable metrics
design_notes: We chose a state-machine approach for progression: WAIT -> OBSERVE -> EVALUATE -> PROGRESS/ROLLBACK. This keeps step logic deterministic and simplifies retries.

Two progression modes: TIME (advance after X minutes if gates pass) and METRIC (advance when sample size and metric thresholds satisfied). METRIC mode uses sliding windows with min_sample_count to avoid noisy decisions.

Traffic splits support weighted buckets and attribute-based routing via match expressions (e.g., region == 'eu' && user_tier == 'enterprise'). This allows partial regional canaries and sticky sessions for user cohorts.
Auto-rollback triggers: absolute error-rate delta > 0.5% OR relative error-rate multiplier > 2x OR P95 latency increase > 200ms OR model-quality regression on evaluation set (A/B eval) > 3%.
We will reuse existing metrics ingestion from the Console pipeline; a new canonical metrics view (per-release, per-step) will be added to Grafana and the Console UI.

Backwards compatibility: curator outputs a routing contract (model-version -> variant-id) consumed by the runtime rather than directly mutating runtime topology. This allows Dedicated/Private deployments to implement the contract locally.
Security: rollout control plane operations will be audited; curator requests require RBAC rollout:write permission. No secrets are stored in the curator service.
implementation_plan: Router integration: implement contract consumer in runtime and test on staging — 5d
Guardrail engine: implement threshold evaluator and state machine — 4d
Console: metrics visualization and manual override buttons (DES-209) — 3d
E2E tests: fault-injection scenarios and metric-based progression tests — 3d
Canary run: small internal rollout to infra-team + runbook and on-call training — 1d
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL parsing and validation (invalid schedules, missing gates)
Simulated traffic harness to validate weighting, shadowing, and sticky cohort routing
Chaos tests: induce 5xx on canary model to validate auto-rollback within expected window
Metric noise tests: ensure min_sample_count prevents premature advancement
Integration tests with Dedicated staging cluster to validate contract-based routing
rollout_notes: Start with a 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% linear time-based default profile for hosted API
Default guardrail presets for low-latency, high-throughput models: P95 latency delta cap 200ms, error-rate delta cap 0.5%, min_sample_count 200 requests/step
For embedding-only models, add embedding-similarity regression guard (cosine decline > 2% on eval set) as optional gate
Rollback cadence: fast rollback (immediate) if >2x errors OR soft rollback (step back one) if metric breach is marginal
Shadow mode: allow mirrored traffic to a candidate for up to 24h for behavioral analysis without user impact
